newsitem.title: FRANCE: France looks for new spending cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: France looks for new spending cuts - paper.

text.p: The French government is considering making new spending cuts in its traditional end-of-year revised budget for 1996, financial daily Les Echos said on Wednesday.

It said the revised budget, likely to be presented to the cabinet on November 13, would be designed to ensure the government met its target of limiting the central government budget deficit to 288 billion francs this year.
Officials were not immediately available for comment.
Les Echos said the government needed to find ways of meeting it target despite lower-than-expected revenues and higher-than-expected spending on some areas.

It said the government was also considering whether to pay its telephone bills to France Telecom after its legal status is changed or before. Its legal status will be changed in January ahead of partial privatisation. The state owed some 2.5 billion francs to France Telecom in telephone bills, it said.

The government also needed to find funds to finance capital injections due for a number of state-owned companies. These injections are in theory supposed to be funded with the revenues from privatisations.
Les Echos said the government would either top up this year's privatisation receipts by selling some of the stakes it still holds in private companies, or delay the capital injections into next year.
